_about: Profiles of meta decks. Text fields are shown on the site. 'model' feeds the matchup simulator (assets/js/sim.js); its numbers are estimates from card text and sample lists, not measured data.

mega-rayquaza.name: Mega Rayquaza
mega-rayquaza.summary: Delta Reign's new deck: a Colorless box of Mega Rayquaza ex, Mega Kangaskhan ex and Talonflame ex, running Fire and Lightning Energy and Legendary Pyroduct.
plan: Mega Rayquaza ex (Basic, 280 HP) Storm Emerald does 50 damage for each Fire and Lightning Energy attached to all of your Pokémon, so its damage grows every turn.
Ruler's Roar attaches a Basic Energy from the top 4 cards when Rayquaza is benched; Energy Switch moves it where needed.
Mega Kangaskhan ex draws 2 from the Active Spot (Run Errand) and hits for 200 plus 50 per heads.
Talonflame ex (Stage 2, 280 HP) moves straight from hand to bench once any Mega Evolution Pokémon ex is in play (Excited Dive). Talon Hunt does 150 and searches 2 cards.
Legendary Pyroduct turns off the abilities of Evolution Pokémon for both players.
beatIt: Its Megas give up 3 prizes each, so two KOs on Mega ex win the game.
Lightning hits Rayquaza and Talonflame for double; Fighting hits Kangaskhan for double.

Team Rocket's Watchtower (Colorless Pokémon have no abilities) blanks Ruler's Roar and Run Errand; Excited Dive still works, because it is used from the hand. N's Zoroark runs it and wins this matchup 61% of the time.
If your engine is an Evolution Pokémon's ability, carry a stadium to bump Pyroduct.

dragapult.name: Dragapult
dragapult.summary: Stage 2 Dragon that hits for 200 and spreads 6 damage counters on the bench every turn. The most-played deck online, and 6 of the top 10 at LAIC.
plan: Dreepy, then Drakloak (Recon Directive digs 2 cards deep each turn), then Dragapult ex on your third turn; the list has no Rare Candy.
Phantom Dive does 200 to the Active and puts 6 damage counters on the bench in any split, setting up multi-KO turns.
Hammer builds add 4 Crushing Hammer; Munkidori moves 3 damage counters from its side to yours.
Meowth ex and Fezandipiti ex are the usual support ex.
beatIt: No Weakness and 320 HP: plan two-hit KOs, or use single-prize attackers so its 200 overkills.
Keep 60-HP-or-less Pokémon off your bench: Phantom Dive farms them for free prizes.
Hide 'n' Sneak Pokémon (Dhelmise deck) ignore the bench damage counters; Dhelmise wins 56% here.
Gust Drakloak or Dreepy before Dragapult ex lands.

engine.evolved: Drakloak's Recon Directive and Dudunsparce's draw

basic-box.name: Basic Box
basic-box.summary: All-Basic toolbox: Mega Kangaskhan ex, Teal Mask Ogerpon ex, Lillie's Clefairy ex, Raging Bolt ex and more, with Area Zero Underdepths for a bigger bench.
plan: No evolutions to build, so it attacks from turn 1 going second.
Picks the right attacker for each target: Raging Bolt ex for huge KOs, Lillie's Clefairy ex against Dragons, Kangaskhan for raw damage.
Crispin and Energy Switch power attackers fast; Cyrano finds them.
beatIt: Every Pokémon gives up 2 or 3 prizes, so single-prize attackers win the trade.
Crustle's Mysterious Rock Inn walls every ex attack; Crustle wins this 71% of the time.
Energy and hand disruption hurt it: its attackers need several Energy each.

slowking.name: Slowking
slowking.summary: Psychic deck built on a single-prize attacker. Slowking's Seek Inspiration discards your top card and, if it is a Pokémon without a Rule Box, uses one of its attacks.
plan: Slowpoke into Slowking (Stage 1, 120 HP) on turn 2.
The attacks it copies: Kyurem's Trifrost (110 to three of your opponent's Pokémon), Metagross's Metallic Hammer (150) and Zeraora's Thunder Raid (210 to a benched Pokémon ex).
Ciphermaniac's Codebreaking and Academy at Night help control the top card.
Mega Kangaskhan ex is the backup attacker.
beatIt: Darkness hits Slowking for double; N's Zoroark wins 56% here.
Talonflame Dusknoir wins 69%: snipes plus big hits outpace the 1-prize trade.
Seek Inspiration whiffs when the top card is not a non-ex Pokémon. Hand disruption breaks their top-deck setup.

ogerpon-meganium-hydrapple.name: Ogerpon Meganium Hydrapple
ogerpon-meganium-hydrapple.summary: Teal Mask Ogerpon ex hits harder with more Energy, Meganium's Wild Growth makes every Basic Grass Energy count as two, and Hydrapple ex closes games.
plan: Teal Mask Ogerpon ex attaches Grass Energy from hand and draws; Myriad Leaf Shower scales with Energy on both Active Pokémon.
Meganium (Stage 2, 160 HP) online on turn 2 or 3 doubles every Basic Grass Energy.
Hydrapple ex (330 HP) is the late-game attacker; Forest of Vitality speeds up evolving.
beatIt: Fire Weakness on Ogerpon, Meganium and Hydrapple.
Gust and KO Meganium (1 prize) to cut their damage in half.
Crustle walls its ex attackers and wins 69% here.

engine.evolved: Meganium's Wild Growth and Hydrapple ex's Ripening Charge

alakazam-dudunsparce.name: Alakazam Dudunsparce
alakazam-dudunsparce.summary: Single-prize Stage 2. Alakazam's Powerful Hand places 2 damage counters on the Active for each card in your hand; Dudunsparce and Psychic Draw keep the hand big.
plan: Rare Candy into Alakazam (140 HP) on turn 2; Psychic Draw draws 3 when it evolves.
Damage counters ignore Weakness, Resistance and damage-prevention effects.
Every Pokémon is single-prize, so it wins long prize trades.
beatIt: Hand disruption shrinks its damage (Unfair Stamp, Judge, Team Rocket's tricks).
Darkness hits Alakazam for double.
Crustle wins 71% here on Limitless.

sample.event: E4MC Modern Mondays, Delta Reign legal (1st of 37)

engine.evolved: Psychic Draw and Dudunsparce's draw, which keep the hand big

n-zoroark.name: N's Zoroark
n-zoroark.summary: N's Zoroark ex copies the attacks of benched N's Pokémon (Night Joker) and draws with Trade. Team Rocket's Watchtower shuts off Colorless Pokémon abilities. Won LAIC 2026–27.
plan: N's Zorua into N's Zoroark ex (280 HP) on turn 2, then Trade (discard 1, draw 2) every turn.
Night Joker uses a benched N's Zekrom's attacks for two Darkness Energy, usually Rampaging Thunder for 250 (that Zoroark then can't attack next turn).
Munkidori moves damage counters onto your Pokémon; Watchtower blanks Colorless abilities.
beatIt: Grass hits Zoroark ex for double; Ogerpon decks win 74% here.
280 HP and 2 prizes: you need three KOs, so line up OHKOs.
Crustle walls Zoroark ex and wins 69%.

mega-excadrill.name: Mega Excadrill
mega-excadrill.summary: Metal Stage 1 Mega with 340 HP. Maximum Drilling does 330 with 2 extra Energy attached; a Beldum line and Team Rocket's Petrel support it.
plan: Drilbur into Mega Excadrill ex, with a Beldum, Metang and Metagross line beside it and 16 Metal Energy.
Maximum Drilling: 200, or 330 with 2 extra Energy.
Undermine (90, discard the top 2 cards of their deck) also mills, which matters against walls like Crustle.
beatIt: Fire Weakness.
A 3-prize Mega: two KOs win the game.
Ogerpon decks win 61% here despite Grass Resistance.

dhelmise.name: Dhelmise
dhelmise.summary: Single-prize Psychic deck built on Hide 'n' Sneak Pokémon (Poltchageist, Shuppet, Banette), which ignore the effects of your attacks and abilities. Dhelmise's Vengeful Anchor does 170 once 4 of them are in the discard.
plan: Get 4 Hide 'n' Sneak Pokémon into the discard to power Vengeful Anchor (30 + 140).
Banette's Puppet Pull (80 and search any card) bridges the early turns.
Bench damage counters and snipes can't touch Hide 'n' Sneak Pokémon.
beatIt: Darkness hits Dhelmise and Banette for double.
Big ex attackers outrace it: Mega Rayquaza wins 70% and Talonflame Dusknoir 76%.
Dhelmise itself has no Hide 'n' Sneak, so it can still be gusted and damaged normally.

talonflame-dusknoir.name: Talonflame Dusknoir
talonflame-dusknoir.summary: Talonflame ex attacks every turn off a single Ignition Energy while Dusknoir's Cursed Blast puts 13 damage counters on any Pokémon (Dusknoir is then Knocked Out and gives up 1 prize). Mega Kangaskhan ex draws cards and lets Talonflame ex drop straight onto the bench.
plan: Mega Kangaskhan ex sits in the Active Spot to draw 2 a turn (Run Errand). With a Mega Evolution Pokémon ex in play, Talonflame ex moves from hand straight to the bench (Excited Dive).
Cursed Blast plus an attack makes two-KO turns or picks off benched ex.

Ignition Energy provides three Energy on an Evolution Pokémon and is discarded at the end of the turn, so Talon Hunt (150, then search 2 cards) costs one card a turn. Jamming Tower turns off Pokémon Tools.
beatIt: Each Cursed Blast hands you a prize. Count those in your race.
Fighting hits Kangaskhan for double; Lightning hits Talonflame for double.
N's Zoroark wins 70% and Dragapult Dudunsparce 73% on Limitless.

crustle.name: Crustle
crustle.summary: Crustle (150 HP) takes no damage from Pokémon ex attacks (Mysterious Rock Inn). Eri, Xerosic's Machinations and Gravity Gemstone grind the opponent down while Superb Scissors (120) or Mega Kangaskhan ex take the prizes.
plan: Dwebble's Ascension evolves itself into Crustle; Lumiose City and Buddy-Buddy Poffin get Dwebble down.
Keep a Crustle Active against Pokémon ex decks: Mysterious Rock Inn prevents all their attack damage.
Eri discards two Items from their hand, Xerosic's Machinations cuts it to 3, and Gravity Gemstone makes retreating cost more.
Growing Grass Energy (+20 HP), Hero's Cape, Spiky Energy and Jumbo Ice Cream keep Crustle alive against single-prize attackers.
beatIt: Single-prize attackers ignore the wall: Rocket's Honchkrow wins 75% online and Slowking 57%.
Mysterious Rock Inn is an Ability on an Evolution Pokémon, so Legendary Pyroduct turns it off. Mega Rayquaza, which plays four, wins 64%.
Crustle is Weak to Fire, and Mega Excadrill's Undermine mills them in a long game: Excadrill wins 74%.

festival-lead.name: Festival Lead
festival-lead.summary: Single-prize Grass aggro. With Festival Grounds in play, Dipplin and Seaking can attack twice a turn (Festival Lead), and Dipplin's Do the Wave does 20 for each of your benched Pokémon. Thwackey searches any card each turn while a Festival Lead Pokémon is Active.
plan: Fill the bench fast: Do the Wave does 20 per benched Pokémon, so five benched is 100, twice.
Festival Grounds must be in play for the second attack; play one every turn you can.
Thwackey's Boom Boom Groove searches any card while Dipplin or Seaking is Active.
Gladion's Final Battle (your last card in hand) adds 80 to each attack; Brave Bangle adds 30 against a Pokémon ex. Rabsca protects your bench from attacks.
beatIt: Remove Festival Grounds and they attack once a turn: any Stadium you play replaces it.
Its attackers have 80 to 110 HP, so small hits Knock them Out. Dragapult wins 64% online.
Talonflame Dusknoir wins 70% and Mega Excadrill 67%.

engine.evolved: Festival Lead (two attacks a turn), Thwackey's Boom Boom Groove and Rabsca's Spherical Shield

dragapult-dudunsparce.name: Dragapult Dudunsparce
dragapult-dudunsparce.summary: Dragapult ex with a heavier Dudunsparce engine: Dudunsparce draws 3, and Dudunsparce ex's Tenacious Tail does 60 for each Pokémon ex your opponent has in play. Maximus Sandoval's 30th-place LAIC list still runs four Crushing Hammer.
plan: Same Phantom Dive plan as Dragapult: Dreepy, Drakloak, Dragapult ex on your third turn.
Dudunsparce's Run Away Draw tops up the hand when Recon Directive isn't enough.
Dudunsparce ex's Tenacious Tail (one Energy) punishes benches full of Pokémon ex.
Rosa's Encouragement puts two Energy from the discard back on a Stage 2 when you are behind on prizes.
beatIt: The same answers as Dragapult: Lillie's Clefairy ex, Hide 'n' Sneak and Battle Cage.
Straight Dragapult wins 55% of these games online, and Mega Lucario 59%.
Dudunsparce ex gives up 2 prizes: Boss's Orders it.

engine.evolved: Drakloak's Recon Directive and Dudunsparce's Run Away Draw

lopunny-dudunsparce.name: Lopunny Dudunsparce
lopunny-dudunsparce.summary: Mega Lopunny ex (330 HP) does 230 for one Energy when it moved from the bench to the Active Spot this turn. Dudunsparce's Run Away Draw, used from the Active Spot, draws 3 and leaves the Spot to Lopunny. Mega Froslass ex does 50 for each card in your opponent's hand.
plan: Fan Rotom's Fan Call (your first turn only) finds Buneary and Dunsparce.

Gale Thrust does 60, plus 170 if Mega Lopunny ex moved from your bench to the Active Spot this turn. Dudunsparce's Run Away Draw from the Active Spot draws 3 and shuffles Dudunsparce away, so the Lopunny you promote counts.
Air Balloon on Lopunny makes the retreat into Dudunsparce free: one Lopunny can attack for 230 every turn.
Mega Froslass ex's Resentful Refrain does 50 for each card in their hand, and Wally's Compassion heals a Mega completely.
beatIt: Mega Lopunny ex is Weak to Fighting; Mega Lucario wins 60% online.
Both attackers are Megas: two Knock Outs are six prizes.
Keep your hand small against Mega Froslass ex. Dragapult wins 65% of these games online.

engine.colorless: Dudunsparce's Run Away Draw and Fan Rotom's Fan Call

mega-lucario.name: Mega Lucario
mega-lucario.summary: Mega Lucario ex (Stage 1, 340 HP) hits for 270 with Mega Brave, or 130 with Aura Jab while putting up to three Fighting Energy from the discard onto the bench. Lunatone and Solrock draw and chip; Premium Power Pro adds 30.
plan: Riolu into Mega Lucario ex on turn two; Fighting Gong finds Riolu, Lunatone, Solrock or Energy.
Alternate Mega Brave (270, not two turns running) with Aura Jab (130, refuels the bench from the discard).
Lunatone's Lunar Cycle draws 3 for a Fighting Energy while Solrock is in play.
Hariyama's Heave-Ho Catcher pulls a benched Pokémon into the Active Spot the turn it evolves.
beatIt: Mega Lucario ex is Weak to Psychic: Dhelmise wins 80% online and Slowking 68%.
It is a Mega: two Knock Outs on Lucario are six prizes.
Mega Brave can't be used two turns in a row; survive the 270 turn and punish the Aura Jab turn.

rockets-honchkrow.name: Rocket's Honchkrow
rockets-honchkrow.summary: Team Rocket's Honchkrow discards Team Rocket Supporters from your hand for 60 damage each (Rocket Feathers). Twenty Team Rocket Supporters and Team Rocket's Ariana (draw to 8) keep the hand full; Team Rocket's Porygon2 hits for 20 per Team Rocket Supporter in the discard.
plan: Team Rocket's Proton on turn one, even going first, finds three Basic Team Rocket's Pokémon.
Team Rocket's Ariana draws until you hold 8 cards while all your Pokémon are Team Rocket's.
Rocket Feathers: discard four Team Rocket Supporters for 240, five for 300, for two Energy.
Team Rocket's Giovanni swaps your Active and pulls up theirs; Team Rocket's Articuno blocks attack effects on your Basic Team Rocket's Pokémon.
beatIt: Honchkrow (130 HP) and Murkrow (80) are small single-prize Pokémon: anything that does 130 trades evenly.
Festival Lead wins 83% online and Talonflame Dusknoir 72%.
Hand disruption takes away the Supporters it discards for damage.

greninja.name: Greninja
greninja.summary: Greninja ex (Stage 2, 310 HP, a Fighting-type Tera Pokémon) attacks for one Water: Shinobi Blade does 170 and searches your deck for any card. Mirage Barrage discards two Energy for 120 to two Pokémon. Robson Fortes's LAIC list adds Dusknoir, Mega Froslass ex and Mega Starmie ex as a toolbox.
plan: Froakie, then Frogadier (Summoning Jutsu finds three Pokémon), then Greninja ex; Rare Candy and Grand Tree speed it up.
Shinobi Blade every turn for one Water: 170 and any card from your deck.
Mirage Barrage (120 to two Pokémon) sets up double Knock Outs; it costs two Energy off Greninja.
Dusknoir's Cursed Blast, Mega Starmie ex (210, ignoring effects) and Mega Froslass ex cover what Greninja can't.
beatIt: Greninja ex is Weak to Psychic: Dhelmise wins 79% online.
Dragapult wins 61% and Mega Excadrill 67%.
On the bench Greninja ex takes no damage from attacks (Tera), but damage counters still land: Phantom Dive and Cursed Blast work.

dragapult-blaziken.name: Dragapult Blaziken
dragapult-blaziken.summary: Dragapult ex with Blaziken ex as an Energy engine: Seething Spirit attaches a Basic Energy from the discard every turn, so the Energy on a Knocked Out Dragapult comes straight back. Team Rocket's Watchtower turns off Colorless Pokémon's Abilities.
plan: Build the Dreepy and Torchic lines together; Rare Candy skips Combusken.
Blaziken ex's Seething Spirit reattaches Energy from the discard every turn, so the next Dragapult ex can attack the turn it evolves.
Phantom Dive: 200 plus 6 counters on the bench; Munkidori moves 3 more.
Team Rocket's Watchtower turns off Mega Kangaskhan ex, Mega Rayquaza ex, Meowth ex and Dudunsparce.
beatIt: Two Stage 2 lines are slow: early pressure and Boss's Orders on Drakloak or Combusken break it.
Blaziken ex (320 HP) is Weak to Water; Dhelmise wins 59% online and Mega Lucario 57%.
The same answers as Dragapult: Lillie's Clefairy ex, Hide 'n' Sneak and Battle Cage.

engine.evolved: Drakloak's Recon Directive and Blaziken ex's Seething Spirit

sharpedo-toxtricity.name: Sharpedo Toxtricity
sharpedo-toxtricity.summary: Mega Sharpedo ex (330 HP, Retreat 0) does 270 with Hungry Jaws once it has any damage counters on it. Toxtricity's Sinister Surge attaches a Darkness Energy to a benched Sharpedo and puts 2 counters on it, which turns that bonus on.
plan: Carvanha and Toxel early; each turn Sinister Surge powers and damages a benched Sharpedo.
Hungry Jaws (two Darkness): 120, plus 150 if Sharpedo has any damage counters on it.
Pecharunt ex's Subjugating Chains switches a Sharpedo in Poisoned, and Binding Mochi adds 40 while it is Poisoned.
Munkidori moves counters from your damaged Pokémon to theirs; Watchtower and Gravity Mountain pick the matchups you punish.
beatIt: Mega Sharpedo ex is Weak to Grass: the Hydrapple deck wins 76% online.
It is a Mega: two Knock Outs are six prizes. Mega Lucario wins 71%.
Festival Lead's single-prize attackers win 71%.

dragapult-dusknoir.name: Dragapult Dusknoir
dragapult-dusknoir.summary: Dragapult ex plus Dusknoir's Cursed Blast (13 damage counters on any Pokémon, then Dusknoir is Knocked Out). Phantom Dive's bench counters and Cursed Blast add up to Knock Outs Dragapult can't reach alone.
plan: Build the Dreepy and Duskull lines together: Dawn finds a whole line, Hilda an Evolution and an Energy.
Phantom Dive does 200 plus 6 counters; Cursed Blast adds 13 more anywhere (Dusclops: 5).
Telepathic Psychic Energy benches two Basic Psychic Pokémon; Neo Upper Energy powers a Stage 2.
Team Rocket's Watchtower turns off Colorless Pokémon's Abilities.
beatIt: Every Cursed Blast gives you a prize: make them spend Dusknoir on single-prize Pokémon.
Psyduck's Damp turns off Cursed Blast, and Battle Cage stops it on your bench.
Basic Box wins 71% online, Mega Lucario 69% and Dhelmise 67%.

engine.evolved: Drakloak's Recon Directive and Dusknoir's Cursed Blast
